identity.name: Reverso Tribute Duoface
identity.one_liner: A Reverso with a second dial on the back, turning the case-flip mechanism into a functional second time zone display.

narrative.story: For the Reverso's first six decades, the caseback that faces outward when the watch is flipped was blank steel, sometimes engraved but otherwise unused. Jaeger-LeCoultre's Duoface variants put a second dial on that face instead, showing a second time zone independent of the primary dial on the front. It converts the original 1931 case mechanism, built to protect a dial from polo mallets, into a genuine travel complication rather than a purely decorative flip.
narrative.collector_notes: Check which dial is wired as the 'home' time and which is the independently-settable second time zone — the two dials are not symmetric in function, and buyers sometimes assume the watch is a simple reversible pair of identical faces.
